message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value (Standard Conditions) |
|----------|-----------------------------|
| **Atomic Number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Isotopic Forms** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2D or D), Tritium (^3T or T) |
| **Molar Mass** | ~1.008 g·mol⁻¹ (protium); ≈2.014 g·mol⁻¹ (deuterium); ≈3.016 g·mol⁻¹ (tritium) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.0899 kg/m³ (≈0.00009 g/cm³) – lightest gas |
| **Melting Point** | −259.16 °C (−434.5 °F) → solidifies only under high pressure or cryogenic temperatures |
| **Boiling Point** | −252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) – very low; evaporates easily |
| **Critical Temperature** | +33.41 °C (≈306 K) |
| **Critical Pressure** | 12.8 MPa (~127 atm) |
| **Specific Heat Capacity (gas)** | Cp ≈ 28.836 J/(mol·K) at 25 °C |
| **Enthalpy of Vaporisation** | ΔHvap ≈ 27.24 kJ/mol |
| **Ionization Energy** | First IE ≈ 13.598 eV (1312 kJ/mol) – highest among elements due to single valence electron |
| **Electron Affinity** | -72.7 meV (very small negative value) – tends to lose rather than gain electrons |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling scale)** | 2.20 – moderate; higher than many metals but lower than halogens |
| **Reactivity** | Extremely reactive as a reducing agent; forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂). Combines readily with oxygen forming water (exothermic). |
| **Bond Dissociation Energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ/mol (typical covalent bond strength) |
| **Spectral Lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – hallmark of hydrogen’s emission spectrum. |

### Additional Highlights

* **Chemical Behavior**
  * Acts as a one‑electron donor; forms ionic bonds when paired with highly electronegative atoms (forming salts like LiH).
  * In its diatomic form (H₂), it behaves as a nonpolar molecule—no permanent dipole moment.
  * Under extreme conditions (high temperature/pressure), hydrogen becomes metallic—a phase predicted theoretically and observed experimentally around 400 GPa.

* **Physical State Variations**
  * At room temperature and atmospheric pressure, exists solely as a colorless, odorless diatomic gas.
  * Solidified hydrogen requires pressures >100 atm or temperatures below −260 °C; crystalline structures include hexagonal close‑packed (hcp) and face‑centered cubic (fcc).

* **Applications & Significance**
  * Fuel source (hydrogen fuel cells) – produces electricity via electrochemical reaction with oxygen, emitting only water vapor.
  * Industrial feedstock – used in ammonia synthesis (Haber process), methanol production, petroleum refining.
  * Scientific research – benchmark element for quantum mechanics, spectroscopy, astrophysics (stellar composition studies).

---

#### Quick Reference Cheat Sheet

```
• Symbol: H   • Atomic # : 1
• Isotopes: ^1H, ^2D, ^3T
• Boil Pt.: -253 °C    Melt Pt.: -259 °C
• Density @STP: 0.090 kg/m^3
• Ionization Energy: 13.60 eV
• Electronegativity: 2.20
• Bond E(H-H): 436 kJ/mol
• Spectra: Lyman, Balmer, Paschen lines
```

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property!
